title: TradingView-style charts, TPO market profile, footprint, liquidations from 12 exchanges — drawn by a Rust engine in WebAssembly
author: rext88
selftext:
Under the hood: Rust → WASM in a Web Worker, WebGL2 on an OffscreenCanvas, live exchange WebSockets straight to the browser. 155 KB engine. 

Open source (AGPL), self-hostable.

comments.author: QATSAlgo
comments.body:
The broker-adapter idea in the comments would benefit from separating historical bars, the live market stream and private account state, rather than forcing everything through a WebSocket-shaped interface. Also expose history gaps instead of silently treating reconnects as continuous data.



We’re QATS. If a perpetuals-prop adapter is useful to you, try our Trading API docs: [https://quantityproject.github.io/qats-trader-api/](https://quantityproject.github.io/qats-trader-api/) . There are tickers/books/bars, market SSE, and account/risk/order/position operations. It requires a separate integration: there is no WebSocket or private order stream, and the capped history routes are not a gap-free full-history export. Evaluations and initial funded accounts are simulated. I’d keep your exchange footprint feed separate from this execution/account adapter.
